description: Illustrative issuance-maturity scenarios over the CBO baseline horizon. Treasury moves the bill share of marketable debt up or down by 5 percentage points over the first year and the 10-year yield moves with it. Each issuance change runs twice: with the change in the bill stock spread across holders in proportion to their bill holdings, and with banks and foreign accounts taking up the whole change. Financing cost depends on the issuance mix and the yield; the deposit effect depends on who buys or gives up the bills.
boundaries: Illustrative scenario accounting, not a forecast or causal estimate
The 10-year yield shift is a stated assumption, not an estimated response to the issuance change
Holder shares are assumptions about who absorbs the change in the bill stock, not estimated demand

Every scenario puts the TGA on the operating-cash path at each fiscal-year end (within a year it sits below the path by issuance awaiting settlement), so financing-cost differences change the debt rather than the TGA
Foreign holders settle through US banks; banks pay for securities with reserves

calibration.issuance: Bill-share target moves linearly from the package's opening bill share (about 22.5% of marketable debt) by +5 or -5 percentage points between 2026-06-21 and 2027-06-30 and stays there. The lower case returns to the middle of the 15-20% range the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee has recommended; the higher case extends recent bill-heavy issuance.
calibration.rates: Key-rate shift of the nominal curve: zero at two years and below, -25 (shorter) or +25 (longer) basis points at ten years and beyond, log-tenor linear between, from the start of the simulation.
calibration.holders: Proportional cases keep the baseline auction shares, which follow opening holdings of bills and of longer securities. Bank-and-foreign cases give banks and foreign accounts the whole change in the bill stock, in proportion to their baseline bill shares; every other holder keeps its baseline bill holdings in dollars.
